bull_bear.body:
- Net debt ₹118 cr, 0.1x net debt/equity — under-levered (analysts flagged ROE drag).
- **No buyback** despite eased regulations; cash to be deployed into growth capex (vertical integration).
- Dividend policy: 8–12% payout; FY26 payout retained at 8% (FY25 also 8%); ~30% dividend rate (vs 25%). 3 priorities: growth capex, shareholder reward, debt. Surplus beyond capex would lift payout.
- Non-core land parcel monetized (~₹8 cr profit).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Cotton:** Rising prices (₹55k→₹62k/candy); pre-buy bet on continued rise; ~30% import exposure + 11% duty + rupee depreciation (₹90→~96/USD) raise imported cotton & spares cost.
- **Demand / pass-through:** Big risk = whether downstream (fabric/garment) can absorb higher spreads amid inflation; China demand already tapering since March; Europe muted.
- **Spread sustainability:** ₹148/kg visible only through Q1 FY27; beyond depends on West Asia (US-Iran) conflict, fuel/gas, geopolitics.
- **Macro:** US-Iran conflict disrupting trade routes (shipment delays, logistics cost); volatile energy markets.
- **Working capital / ROE:** Elevated WC (~135–140 days; mgmt target 110–120); receivables +43% (revenue growth + earlier loose payment discipline). OCF down YoY (inventory + receivables).
- **Margin gap vs peers:** Ambika Cotton ~35% EBITDA vs GHCL ~30% (per analyst framing) — GHCL early in vertical-integration journey.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic. Confident on near-term spreads (Q1) and structural FTA/China+1 tailwinds; candid about pass-through risk, China tapering, fuel/geopolitics, and being early in vertical-integration vs peers. R.S. Jalan closing: visibility of optimism returning after long headwind; on track for FY29–30 ₹2,000 cr + 15–18% EBITDA + double-digit ROCE.
bull_bear.title: Mgmt tone

bull_bear.body:
- Q4 yarn VOLUME actually dipped QoQ (~10,800→~10,400 tons); EBITDA growth was spread-driven, not volume-driven — analyst pushed on gross-margin vs spread mismatch (answer: unitized vs absolute, volume slightly lower).
- US exposure is INDIRECT (via fabric manufacturers), not direct — tariff resolution still mattered for demand.
- China bought Indian yarn in Q4 due to low Indian yarn prices + Chinese cotton acreage cut — a transient, now tapering tailwind.
- No inventory gains booked despite cotton rise; the ~₹8 cr land-sale gain is the real one-off boosting reported PAT.
- "Doubling revenue" in PPT = from original ~₹1,000 cr base to ~₹2,000 cr (NOT doubling current ₹1,335 cr to ₹2,600 cr) — mgmt clarified.
- ROCE only now becoming an explicit management KPI (improved ~1% this year; target double-digit).
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious points

bull_bear.body:
- "Strong balance sheet supports sustainable growth" is the only balance-sheet framing offered; the deck does not discuss dividends, buybacks or leverage.
- Reinvestment is channelled through the Rs. 1,035 Cr Tamil Nadu MoU programme, of which ~Rs. 675 Cr is already invested.
- Return focus: "Our focus remains on operational discipline, cost efficiency and working capital optimization, with scale and vertical integration expected to drive higher RoCE and sustainable growth", echoed as "scale, mix and integration upside supporting RoCE".
- Disclosed one-off: "FY26 Financials include one time gain of Rs. 8.59 Cr. on account of sale of non-strategic land."
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Significant renewable energy portfolio (65 MW wind and solar in Tamil Nadu) provides a structural cost advantage and de-risks EBITDA margins from fuel-price volatility
- Deliberate diversification into value-added speciality yarns and forward integration into fabric: fabric share of revenue rose to 13.7% in FY26 from nil in FY19
- Deep, strategic long-term relationships with a select customer base built on quality/rigorous quality control, supporting pricing beyond commodity price alone
- Export mix has grown to 10.2% of revenue in FY26 from 5.5% in FY19, benefiting from China Plus One diversification and disruption in competing garment nations such as Bangladesh
- In-house expertise in cotton market dynamics and disciplined raw-material procurement/inventory management cited as a competitive differentiator
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Cotton price volatility and constrained availability of high-quality cotton — Management explicitly flags cotton price volatility and constraints on high-quality cotton availability as a source of unpredictability; domestic cotton prices surged from Rs 55,000 per candy in December 2025 to Rs 62,000 per candy by March 2026, directly affecting the company's key raw material cost.
- Cotton crop yield risk from changing weather patterns — Management identifies changing weather patterns adversely affecting cotton crop yields as a monitored risk, given cotton is the primary raw material input for spinning operations.
- Global economic uncertainty and evolving tariff conditions — Flagged as a market challenge creating uncertainty in the operating environment, relevant given the company's export exposure and reliance on trade policy stability (e.g. FTAs with UK/EU).
- Global trade-route and logistics disruption — The US-Iran conflict disrupted traditional trade routes in FY26, causing shipment delays and a sharp escalation in logistics and shipping costs that resounded across the global textile supply chain.
- Geopolitical risk amplifying energy price volatility — Sustained hostilities in the Middle East have periodically amplified geopolitical risk premiums, pushing energy prices higher and straining traditional trade routes, which is relevant to a manufacturer with an international footprint and material energy costs.
- Technological, geopolitical and regulatory/environmental change — The Risk Management Committee explicitly recognises that technological advancements, geopolitical developments, and evolving regulatory and environmental requirements have significant bearing on the business and are systematically managed as enterprise risks.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- Q4 strong on both volume AND pricing; knitting and weaving both improved; domestic demand improved meaningfully.
- Demand triggers: (a) resolution of US reciprocal/penalty tariffs (India sells to US indirectly via fabric makers) unleashed demand; (b) India-EU FTA → European inquiries concretized; (c) China yarn demand spike in Q4 (low Indian yarn prices + Chinese cotton acreage cut) — now tapering since March; (d) steady domestic QoQ/YoY growth.
- Exports ~14% of Q4 top line (up QoQ). Europe muted ~1–1.5 yrs but steady; Bangladesh strong; US only indirect (via fabric manufacturers).
- FTAs (UK/EU) not yet executed but supply chains reorienting to India; UK/EU customers placing trial orders.

- Two state-of-the-art manufacturing units with cutting-edge textile machinery, both located in Tamil Nadu, producing "high-quality tailor-made yarns, catering to domestic and international markets".

business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [India-UK CETA] The UK FTA "Commenced on 15th July" and removes a ~8-12% tariff disadvantage; the deck's tariff table shows Yarn & Fabrics and Garments moving from a pre-FTA 8-12% to a post-FTA 0%.
- [UK opportunity] Deck cites India's textile & apparel exports to the UK at US$1.9 Bn currently rising to US$3.5-4.0 Bn in 3-5 years, an "Incremental Opportunity US$ 1.5 - 2.0 Bn", with "Large headroom for growth as India's share in a ~US$30Bn UK market has been low".
- [FTA pipeline] Oman came into effect 3rd June with 5-10% duty removed for yarn, fabric & garment; New Zealand agreed (3-5% to 0% on yarn/fabric, ~10% to 0% for garments, ~8-10% landed-cost reduction); EU FTA agreed and implementing in 2027 (0% vs earlier ~8-12%); Canada (from 16-18%), Peru (10-16%), Israel (0-12%) and GCC (~5%) under negotiation.
- [US tariffs] "Tariffs reset ~10%" with "20%+ US cotton input = 0% duty on exports; vs 10% with Indian cotton. Mills can optimize per order."
- [Cotton policy & prices] "The 11% cotton import duty waived from 1st June is effective till 30th October 2026"; Indian cotton prices near global parity with a gap of ~0.5c/lb (79.5c vs 80.0c/lb), yarn-cotton spread expanded in Q1FY27, and acreage/output expected to rise next season.

outlook.body:
- Expand product basket, grow the value-added segment, realign the customer base toward more strategic relationships, deepen penetration of the fabric market, and continue driving operational excellence across manufacturing facilities
- Forward-integrate from pure spinning into knitted and greige fabric / value-added products to capture higher realisations as the segment scales
- Continue deploying renewable energy assets as a parallel sustainability priority, targeting a minimum of 75 to 80 percent of total energy requirements from green sources
- Core operating principles guiding growth: disciplined cash conversion, deep in-house expertise in cotton market dynamics, supply chain resilience, investment in value-added processing, a culture of product and process innovation, and an unwavering focus on customer satisfaction
- Company has adopted a formal Dividend Distribution Policy as part of its broader corporate governance policy framework (alongside policies on Board Diversity, Materiality, Related Party Transactions, Risk Management, Whistle Blower and Nomination & Remuneration), governing the Board's dividend recommendations. outlook.body: GHCL Textiles has committed to invest over Rs 1,000 crores in capacity and capability, of which Rs 600 crores had already been deployed; during FY26 the company commissioned 25,000 new spindles, 15 knitting machines, and 3 MW of additional green energy capacity, a step towards forward-integrating operations from spinning into value-added fabric to capture higher realisations. Manufacturing operations are located at Paravai, Madurai and Manaparai, Tiruchirapalli in Tamil Nadu, with modern spinning facilities comprising 2.25 lakh ring spindles, 3,320 rotors, 5,760 TFO spindles, 5 Airjet Spinning machines and 15 knitting machines, underpinned by a 65 MW wind and solar renewable energy portfolio. During the year the company incurred Rs 67.93 crores on growth and maintenance capital expenditure, financed through internal accruals, which further strengthened capacity, forward integration into knitting/fabric, and solar energy capacity.

outlook.body:
- Accelerating 'China Plus One' diversification and socio-political disruption in competing garment nations such as Bangladesh continue to redirect Readymade Garment orders toward India, strengthening demand outlook for Indian yarn and fabric manufacturers
- Progressive execution of Free Trade Agreements with the UK, the EU and other key markets expected to deliver a sustained demand tailwind and improved market access for Indian exporters
- Rising discretionary incomes and rapid urbanisation provide a stable domestic demand floor for yarn and fabric, cushioning temporary international headwinds
- Structural industry forces expected to bolster India's export opportunity: increased online retailing, an accelerating shift from cotton to man-made fibre, strong growth in technical textiles, and ongoing migration of global textile production outside China
- Expanding renewable energy footprint is intended to materially de-risk EBITDA margins against global energy/fuel price volatility
- Management flags market challenges creating uncertainty: global economic uncertainty, evolving tariff conditions, changing weather patterns adversely affecting cotton crop yields, cotton price volatility, and constraints on availability of high-quality cotton

thesis (one line): A spinning-heavy yarn player de-risking via vertical integration into knitted/processed "ready-to-cut" fabric, riding an FY26 spread upcycle (₹123→₹148/kg) and FTA/China+1 export tailwinds, with a multi-year ₹2,000 cr revenue + 15–18% EBITDA goal anchored on PM MITRA Park capex by FY29–30.
scorecard:
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | YoY / note |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue | ₹375 cr | +31% YoY |
| EBITDA | ₹52 cr | margin ~13.9% (mgmt cited EBITDA margin up from ~10% to 11.7% — likely on a different/segment basis); FY EBITDA margin ~11.7% |

**FY26 full year:** Revenue ₹1,335 cr (+14% YoY, from ~₹1,170 cr base); EBITDA ₹156 cr (+34% YoY). Fabric = ~12% of FY26 revenue (up from ~8%).

**One-offs (explicit):**
- Other income jumped to ~₹10 cr; ~₹8-point-something cr pre-tax PROFIT from sale of a non-core / non-strategic land parcel (one-time).
- No inventory gains: mgmt explicitly stated NO inventory gain in FY26 / no FDM inventory gain.
guidance (critical):
- **Volume:** No exact volume guidance. FY27 volume uplift mainly from full-year run of new 25,000 spindles (operated only ~2 quarters in FY26), plus 40 knitting machines (15 installed, +25 from Q3 FY27, ~60% landing Q2–Q3). Mgmt: growth "not only from volume" — also product mix/price maximization. New 25k spindle peak quarterly rev ~₹50–60 cr spinning (₹250–300 cr/yr incl. knitting); currently at ~70–75% contribution.
- **Spread:** Q4 spread of **₹148/kg expected to CONTINUE into Q1 FY27** with high visibility ("conservatively certain"); could go up. Beyond Q1 depends on geopolitics/fuel. China yarn demand tapering since March.
- **Capex:** FY27 capex **₹100–120 cr** — ₹35 cr on-ground 10MW solar; ₹15 cr knitting machines; balance PM MITRA Park land + replacement/infra capex. Remaining ~₹300–350 cr (of original ₹1,000 cr plan; ~₹675 cr already deployed) over next 3 yrs, mostly toward **fabric + processing** (ready-to-cut). Asset turn on incremental fabric/processing ~1.5x.
- **Margin:** Normal EBITDA ~15% (10-yr track); targeting **15–18% EBITDA margin** over next 3 yrs via vertical integration + premium product mix + 98–99% utilization. FY27 growth expected "near about" FY26 level (±2% delta).
- **Long-term anchor:** ~**₹2,000 cr revenue** + 15–18% EBITDA by **FY29–FY30** (revenue ~FY29, margin ~FY30). ROCE focus added — aiming for double-digit ROCE (improved ~1% this year).
demand:
- Q4 strong on both volume AND pricing; knitting and weaving both improved; domestic demand improved meaningfully.
- Demand triggers: (a) resolution of US reciprocal/penalty tariffs (India sells to US indirectly via fabric makers) unleashed demand; (b) India-EU FTA → European inquiries concretized; (c) China yarn demand spike in Q4 (low Indian yarn prices + Chinese cotton acreage cut) — now tapering since March; (d) steady domestic QoQ/YoY growth.
- Exports ~14% of Q4 top line (up QoQ). Europe muted ~1–1.5 yrs but steady; Bangladesh strong; US only indirect (via fabric manufacturers).
- FTAs (UK/EU) not yet executed but supply chains reorienting to India; UK/EU customers placing trial orders.
segment (yarn / fabric):
- **Yarn mix:** ~65–70% 100% cotton yarn; ~30–35% synthetic/blended (polyester-rich, cotton-rich, cellulosic blends).
- **Customer mix:** ~40–50% volume to concentrated strategic large brands; ~20–25% to brands via intermediaries/traders (direct brand communication); rest ~20–25% small/medium customers servicing brands.
- **Fabric:** ~12% of FY26 revenue (from 8%); targeting ~15% FY27, 16–18% once 40 machines installed. ~50% of fabric = knitted (in-house); woven stays outsourced. ~15–16 tons/day knitted (~12% of volume). Plan: 40% of yarn sold as yarn, 60% vertically integrated into fabric/processed fabric.
growth / optionality:
- **PM MITRA Park (Virudhunagar, TN):** ~50-acre land allotment received — strategic; to host processing + ready-to-cut fabric; "next phase of scale growth and product integration." Details TBD.
- **Vertical integration → ready-to-cut fabric supplier** is the core vision; ~₹350 cr pending capex skewed to fabric/processing (higher asset turn ~1.5x) to bridge to ₹2,000 cr.
- New 25,000-spindle unit stabilized at optimum utilization; knitting machine expansion underway.
- Rooftop + on-ground solar (energy cost optionality). FY27 = first full year of new capacity benefit.
margins & cost:
- **Cotton:** Prices rose ~₹55,000/candy (Dec '25) → ~₹62,000 currently. Mgmt pre-bought cotton ahead of rise → cost advantage expected as inventory flows through; ~120 days (~4 months) inventory as of 31-Mar; ~25–30% imported cotton, rest domestic. 11% import duty reinstated from January.
- **Power:** 3MW rooftop solar (~₹2 cr/yr full benefit); 10MW on-ground solar commissioning Jul–Aug FY27 (~₹6.5–7 cr full-yr, ~₹4.5 cr in FY27 partial as summer passes).
- **Energy/fuel:** Higher fuel prices pressuring synthetic portfolio + fabric manufacturing cost economics. Mgmt does NOT use gas in processes (no direct gas-availability hit), but value chain inflation a risk.
- EBITDA margin lifted to ~11.7% (Q4); R.S. Jalan: EBITDA up ~29% QoQ even ex one-time income, matching the ₹123→₹148 spread move.
capex:
- ~₹675 cr of original ₹1,000 cr plan deployed; ~₹300–350 cr pending over ~3 yrs (mostly fabric + processing).
- FY27: ₹100–120 cr (₹35 cr 10MW ground solar; ₹15 cr knitting; balance PM MITRA + replacement/infra).
- PM MITRA Park ~50 acres — substantial future capital for processing/ready-to-cut.
capital allocation:
- Net debt ₹118 cr, 0.1x net debt/equity — under-levered (analysts flagged ROE drag).
- **No buyback** despite eased regulations; cash to be deployed into growth capex (vertical integration).
- Dividend policy: 8–12% payout; FY26 payout retained at 8% (FY25 also 8%); ~30% dividend rate (vs 25%). 3 priorities: growth capex, shareholder reward, debt. Surplus beyond capex would lift payout.
- Non-core land parcel monetized (~₹8 cr profit).
risks:
- **Cotton:** Rising prices (₹55k→₹62k/candy); pre-buy bet on continued rise; ~30% import exposure + 11% duty + rupee depreciation (₹90→~96/USD) raise imported cotton & spares cost.
- **Demand / pass-through:** Big risk = whether downstream (fabric/garment) can absorb higher spreads amid inflation; China demand already tapering since March; Europe muted.
- **Spread sustainability:** ₹148/kg visible only through Q1 FY27; beyond depends on West Asia (US-Iran) conflict, fuel/gas, geopolitics.
- **Macro:** US-Iran conflict disrupting trade routes (shipment delays, logistics cost); volatile energy markets.
- **Working capital / ROE:** Elevated WC (~135–140 days; mgmt target 110–120); receivables +43% (revenue growth + earlier loose payment discipline). OCF down YoY (inventory + receivables).
- **Margin gap vs peers:** Ambika Cotton ~35% EBITDA vs GHCL ~30% (per analyst framing) — GHCL early in vertical-integration journey.
mgmt tone: Cautiously optimistic. Confident on near-term spreads (Q1) and structural FTA/China+1 tailwinds; candid about pass-through risk, China tapering, fuel/geopolitics, and being early in vertical-integration vs peers. R.S. Jalan closing: visibility of optimism returning after long headwind; on track for FY29–30 ₹2,000 cr + 15–18% EBITDA + double-digit ROCE.
non-obvious points:
- Q4 yarn VOLUME actually dipped QoQ (~10,800→~10,400 tons); EBITDA growth was spread-driven, not volume-driven — analyst pushed on gross-margin vs spread mismatch (answer: unitized vs absolute, volume slightly lower).
- US exposure is INDIRECT (via fabric manufacturers), not direct — tariff resolution still mattered for demand.
- China bought Indian yarn in Q4 due to low Indian yarn prices + Chinese cotton acreage cut — a transient, now tapering tailwind.
- No inventory gains booked despite cotton rise; the ~₹8 cr land-sale gain is the real one-off boosting reported PAT.
- "Doubling revenue" in PPT = from original ~₹1,000 cr base to ~₹2,000 cr (NOT doubling current ₹1,335 cr to ₹2,600 cr) — mgmt clarified.
- ROCE only now becoming an explicit management KPI (improved ~1% this year; target double-digit).
challenges → beneficiaries:
- China+1 / FTA reorientation (US tariff resolution, India-EU/UK FTAs) → Indian cotton/blended yarn & fabric exporters (GHCL via fabric makers + direct EU/Bangladesh). ⭐
- India cotton structural advantage (2nd-largest producer, low yield = production upside, spinning tech upgrade) → Indian cotton spinners vs global synthetic shift. ✅
- PM MITRA Park infrastructure → integrated textile players co-locating spinning + processing + ready-to-cut. ⭐

capex_expansion.body: GHCL Textiles has committed to invest over Rs 1,000 crores in capacity and capability, of which Rs 600 crores had already been deployed; during FY26 the company commissioned 25,000 new spindles, 15 knitting machines, and 3 MW of additional green energy capacity, a step towards forward-integrating operations from spinning into value-added fabric to capture higher realisations. Manufacturing operations are located at Paravai, Madurai and Manaparai, Tiruchirapalli in Tamil Nadu, with modern spinning facilities comprising 2.25 lakh ring spindles, 3,320 rotors, 5,760 TFO spindles, 5 Airjet Spinning machines and 15 knitting machines, underpinned by a 65 MW wind and solar renewable energy portfolio. During the year the company incurred Rs 67.93 crores on growth and maintenance capital expenditure, financed through internal accruals, which further strengthened capacity, forward integration into knitting/fabric, and solar energy capacity.

management_tone.title: Mgmt tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic. Confident on near-term spreads (Q1) and structural FTA/China+1 tailwinds; candid about pass-through risk, China tapering, fuel/geopolitics, and being early in vertical-integration vs peers. R.S. Jalan closing: visibility of optimism returning after long headwind; on track for FY29–30 ₹2,000 cr + 15–18% EBITDA + double-digit ROCE.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Significant renewable energy portfolio (65 MW wind and solar in Tamil Nadu) provides a structural cost advantage and de-risks EBITDA margins from fuel-price volatility
- Deliberate diversification into value-added speciality yarns and forward integration into fabric: fabric share of revenue rose to 13.7% in FY26 from nil in FY19
- Deep, strategic long-term relationships with a select customer base built on quality/rigorous quality control, supporting pricing beyond commodity price alone
- Export mix has grown to 10.2% of revenue in FY26 from 5.5% in FY19, benefiting from China Plus One diversification and disruption in competing garment nations such as Bangladesh
- In-house expertise in cotton market dynamics and disciplined raw-material procurement/inventory management cited as a competitive differentiator

risks.title: Risks
risks.body:
- **Cotton:** Rising prices (₹55k→₹62k/candy); pre-buy bet on continued rise; ~30% import exposure + 11% duty + rupee depreciation (₹90→~96/USD) raise imported cotton & spares cost.
- **Demand / pass-through:** Big risk = whether downstream (fabric/garment) can absorb higher spreads amid inflation; China demand already tapering since March; Europe muted.
- **Spread sustainability:** ₹148/kg visible only through Q1 FY27; beyond depends on West Asia (US-Iran) conflict, fuel/gas, geopolitics.
- **Macro:** US-Iran conflict disrupting trade routes (shipment delays, logistics cost); volatile energy markets.
- **Working capital / ROE:** Elevated WC (~135–140 days; mgmt target 110–120); receivables +43% (revenue growth + earlier loose payment discipline). OCF down YoY (inventory + receivables).
- **Margin gap vs peers:** Ambika Cotton ~35% EBITDA vs GHCL ~30% (per analyst framing) — GHCL early in vertical-integration journey.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious points
non_obvious.body:
- Q4 yarn VOLUME actually dipped QoQ (~10,800→~10,400 tons); EBITDA growth was spread-driven, not volume-driven — analyst pushed on gross-margin vs spread mismatch (answer: unitized vs absolute, volume slightly lower).

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [India-UK CETA] The UK FTA "Commenced on 15th July" and removes a ~8-12% tariff disadvantage; the deck's tariff table shows Yarn & Fabrics and Garments moving from a pre-FTA 8-12% to a post-FTA 0%.
- [UK opportunity] Deck cites India's textile & apparel exports to the UK at US$1.9 Bn currently rising to US$3.5-4.0 Bn in 3-5 years, an "Incremental Opportunity US$ 1.5 - 2.0 Bn", with "Large headroom for growth as India's share in a ~US$30Bn UK market has been low".
- [FTA pipeline] Oman came into effect 3rd June with 5-10% duty removed for yarn, fabric & garment; New Zealand agreed (3-5% to 0% on yarn/fabric, ~10% to 0% for garments, ~8-10% landed-cost reduction); EU FTA agreed and implementing in 2027 (0% vs earlier ~8-12%); Canada (from 16-18%), Peru (10-16%), Israel (0-12%) and GCC (~5%) under negotiation.
- [US tariffs] "Tariffs reset ~10%" with "20%+ US cotton input = 0% duty on exports; vs 10% with Indian cotton. Mills can optimize per order."
- [Cotton policy & prices] "The 11% cotton import duty waived from 1st June is effective till 30th October 2026"; Indian cotton prices near global parity with a gap of ~0.5c/lb (79.5c vs 80.0c/lb), yarn-cotton spread expanded in Q1FY27, and acreage/output expected to rise next season.

themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.
